fullPassage: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the main component of the Martian atmosphere, but its current level does not produce enough atmospheric pressure to support human activity on the planet. Therefore, scientists are considering ways to increase its concentration in the air. One common idea is to warm up the CO₂ that exists in a frozen state both at the poles and beneath the surface so that it can return to the atmosphere. One of the suggested ways to do this is by detonating high-power explosives on the poles. This would cause a quick melt and would also generate a cloud of dust, darkening the zone around the detonation, thus making solar radiation absorption more efficient. In this way, the area would heat up faster, helping to liquefy the existing water. Unfortunately, analyses of the latest data sent by the various probes indicate that the amount of CO₂ at the poles is not enough to achieve this purpose: vaporising polar ice sheets would only contribute enough CO₂ to double the Martian atmospheric pressure, bringing it to just 1.2% of the Earth's value. If we want to have liquid water at a suitable temperature in a stable way on Mars, an atmospheric pressure similar to the one we have on Earth is required. However, there are also other sources of CO₂ on Mars. Dust particles in the Martian soil contain CO₂, and they could eventually be heated up to release the gas. Scientists estimate that heating the soil could provide up to 4% of the necessary pressure. CO₂ molecules which are intermingled with ice molecules called “clathrate compounds” have also been observed, which upon melting would release CO₂ to the atmosphere. In any case, it is speculated that they would add less than 5% of the required pressure.

det.analysis:
✅ ① increase — frozen — efficient — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② reduce — frozen — efficient (A 반대: 높이다→줄이다)
❌ ③ increase — liquid — efficient (B 반대: 얼어붙은→액체의)
